items.text: REFERRED TO HOUSING, CONSTRUCTION AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT

items.lawCode: Amd §§26-408 & 26-511, NYC Ad Cd; amd §5, Emerg Hous Rent Cont L; amd §10, Emerg Ten Prot Act of 1974
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S1381

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, the
emergency housing rent control law and the emergency tenant protection
act of nineteen seventy-four, in relation to an owner's right to
recover an apartment for personal use


 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :
To provide greater protection to tenants in cases where landlords seek
to recover apartments for their own use.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :
* Amends paragraph 1 of subdivision b of section 26-408 of the
administrative code of the City of New York;

* Amends subparagraph (b) of paragraph 9 of subdivision C of section
26-511 of the administrative code of the City of New York;

* Amends paragraph (a) of subdivision 2 of section 5 of chapter 274 of
the laws of 1946, constituting the emergency housing rent control law,
as amended by chapter 234 of the laws of 1984;

* Amends subdivision a of section 10 of section 4 of chapter 576 of
the laws of 1974, constituting the emergency tenant protection act of
nineteen seventy four, as amended by chapter 234 of the laws of 1984

 JUSTIFICATION :
This bill would make uniform a number of present tenant protections
which exist in the State's four regulatory systems in cases where
landlords seek to recover apartments for their own use or the use of
their family and add additional protections to the rent regulatory
systems.  Under this legislation, landlords in all four systems would
be required to demonstrate immediate and compelling need and good
faith and would have to utilize a recovered housing accommodation as
their primary residence. The bill would also prohibit evictions for
owner occupancy in cases where a landlord sought an apartment for
non-residential use.

The tight rental housing markets which exist in regulated areas of the
state, eviction is often a great hardship for tenants. This measure
would protect tenants against evictions by imposing additional
requirements in cases where landlords sought apartments for their own
personal use. These additional requirements would help ensure that
tenants could only be evicted from their homes when the landlord had
sufficient justification to do so.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
This bill has been introduced in previous legislative sessions.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Immediately and applies to any tenant in possession at or after the
time it takes effect (with additional provisions).

summary: Provides that a landlord receiving possession of a rent regulated housing accommodation for his own use or that of his family must act in good faith, show an immediate and compelling need, and use such housing accommodation as his primary residence or the primary residence of a family member.
title: Limits landlord's rights to recovery of premises for personal use to use as a primary residence
